title: MixEngine package index
description: The single signed document a MixEngine daemon reads to learn what runtimes and services exist and where to fetch them. Versions are never removed from it: a blueprint pinning an old one has to keep working, which is also why no url here may point at an upstream host.

schema.description: Bumped only for a change a current client cannot read. Adding an optional field is not one.

kind.description: php | node | python | ruby | caddy | nginx | mariadb | postgresql | redis | memcached …

version.description: The upstream version exactly as upstream writes it. Not normalised, not zero-padded — it is what the user pinned.

eol.description: Upstream's end of life, when upstream states one. A version past it stays installable and is marked in the GUI; PHP is offered well past its grace period on purpose, see MixEngine's version policy.

artifact.description: One OS/arch build. Everything that varies per platform lives here rather than on the package, because it does vary: a Windows PHP has no php-fpm and needs a VC++ redistributable, and neither statement is true of the same version on Linux.

url.description: A release asset of this repository. Never an upstream URL — upstreams prune, and the index promises they do not.

provides.description: Executable name -> path inside the archive. A map rather than a list because the daemon needs to know where each binary is, and a borrowed archive keeps its publisher's layout rather than being rearranged into ours.

requires.description: Preconditions the daemon checks before installing, and prompts about rather than silently satisfying.

vcredist.description: Per branch, not per runtime: PHP 7.0-7.1 are VC14, 7.2-7.3 VC15, 7.4-8.3 VS16, 8.4+ VS17.

extension_dir.description: Where dynamically loadable extensions live inside the archive, relative to its root. Present whenever the runtime can load any; the generated config always sets this explicitly, because upstream PHP for Windows bakes an absolute C:\php\ext that would otherwise be consulted by accident on a machine where it happens to exist.

extensions.description: What this build can offer. The split is not cosmetic: a static extension cannot be turned off, and a shared one has to be present on disk before it can be turned on.

static.description: Compiled in. Always loaded, never disableable.

shared.description: Loadable modules shipped inside this archive.

enabled.description: Which of `shared` an installer is expected to switch on, so that the cells of one version behave alike. It exists because Windows and Unix cannot express the same decision the same way: curl, openssl, mbstring, intl, gd, zip, sodium, sqlite3 and fileinfo are compiled into the Unix builds and are loadable modules on Windows, and no Windows build exists with them static. A subset of `shared`; saying which extensions are present never said this.
